![](https://db.lilnouns.wtf/api/funding/images/QmSmRPK5g1Qm4Zxhbpsr4LNhidm1FUPFyCpEqyyTmGtQHk)
**Who is this guy???**
My name is Jeremiah "JMi" Wesley and I've had a love for smash that's extended about my entire life. I am originally from Dallas Texas, however I currently reside in Okinawa Japan. I've wanted to compete in all smash titles but ive never had the opportunity do to the expense of travel, that being amplified once I came to Japan. I believe I would be an incredible representative for Nouns at the event! I would like to compete in not only SSBM but SSBU as well :)

**Background**

Even though I have not had the greatest success in SSBM, I have also played the other smash titles as well, such as SSBU, P+ and SSF2. SSF2 being the one I've had the most success in as I was ranked Top 10 in the world. (Yes, i mean super smash flash 2)
![](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1040024656750575717/1152797335353561160/45_8_2.png?ex=66f0d62e&is=66ef84ae&hm=8e2d21f463384acb007d60e0ac2c235bac002118225ff6438cddb2eeebbad9c3&)

![](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1040024656750575717/1258107344269738085/10.png?ex=66f04f45&is=66eefdc5&hm=7bffa17ca6bc6e67085e555a1fa3f2cbbc4ab3f4f31795d219806a2cce12e447&)

There are other great smash players who have came from SSF2 such as LunarySSF2 who has excelled in Europe, and Dany2Theny from Tennessee who has succeeded in SSBU. I strive to be like both of them and break into a bigger title and soon make a name for myself.

I started playing SSBM at the release of slippi and it was one of the most impactful things to happen to me. I had always been a spectator of the game, i just never had been able to invest time into it due to not having a controller and not having access to my local scene. Slippi, of course, was able to change that and ever since then i've been heavily invested into the game and have had the goal of ONE DAY being a top player (i know the journey will be long)

Also I started playing slippi on keyboard so when it was time to eventually play the game in person, I started on a custom made box-style controller that a friend (VerminKnight) made for me. It is the same layout of controls I used for SSF2 and made the transition significantly easier

a clip of what it looks like can be seen here:
[https://x.com/jmidoesstuff/status/1827915582097997905](https://x.com/jmidoesstuff/status/1827915582097997905)

**Community** **and Impact**

Community has always been big thing for me. No matter where I am and what i'm doing i like to leave an impact on whoever is there. Seeing nouns and extended and reach out to the broader areas of the community like us here in Asia is inspiring as its the level of outreach i strive to have one day.

![](https://db.lilnouns.wtf/api/funding/images/QmSmRPK5g1Qm4Zxhbpsr4LNhidm1FUPFyCpEqyyTmGtQHk)

proposals.content:
# Who am I?

My name is Ryan and I’m from the Philippines. I go by Yetis Exist. I’m currently the best player in Southeast Asia (just know when i say this, this does not include Japan which is part of East Asia technically), and have been rank 1 in the Philippines Power Rankings with my Fox since 2020. This is a picture of me below from when I thought I sd'd the same time I killed my opponent in a last stock game.

![](https://db.lilnouns.wtf/api/funding/images/QmUMEku4ZBVTLQK5HHVtCh77HtswLmRmqw5dtEG1dc22CG)

A few of you may have seen my YouTube videos showcasing Melee talent in the Philippines, Southeast Asia, and neighboring Asian regions. You might recognize the thumbnail below that I made for my video about the top Japanese player Inngenn, for example.

![](https://db.lilnouns.wtf/api/funding/images/QmRYMmY3Nu39AJMq7K71r2gjUp1tr9hAxzzHbd2VnAat3L)

# My Grind To Top 100 Journey

Earlier this year I started a YouTube series on my channel called “From Noob To Top 100” where I aim to document my strategies, key moments, and grind to Top 100. I‘m hoping that by applying to this, Don’t Park On The Grass will be one of the events I can attend in my journey. I know for sure it will be an extremely valuable experience! It would be a privilege and honor to represent Asia at this event.

![](https://db.lilnouns.wtf/api/funding/images/QmV6TpUfkU83y3PEr7GpncFs7nJXy1eqacbKAVsq4yqi3T)

# My Results

In terms of majors or super majors, I’ve really only ever attended Genesis 9 in 2023, achieving 257th place losing to Deez and Studebacher Hoch. But I am confident that I’ve improved a lot since then and I’m confident I can do better this time around! For local/online events, I have won the vast majority of the Philippine local and online events I’ve attended since 2020 and got 1st place in the SEA League. 

# My Wins:

- Inngenn
- Massun
- tvd (or Lemon)
- vugzi
- Vivi
- 10QuidShoes
- CptNebula
- Sala

# Being a T.O.

Other than competing, I am also a tournament organizer in my region. I’ve hosted or been involved in most of the online events in the region since 2020 And I’ve been the main tournament organizer for locals in the Philippines. Furthermore, I have tried very hard to grow the community in Asia and give back as much as possible. Although it has been pretty challenging, it has always been an exciting endeavor to pursue and something I am proud of!

# Shoutouts and Thank Yous!

I just want to say that I am grateful for this opportunity and I’m sure whoever the 2 winners are will 100% be deserving of it! I want to give a shoutout to the Japanese Melee scene and my two favorite Japanese players, Inngenn and Hutuka! I want to shoutout the Middle Eastern Melee community! Hi Steel Rhydon, Lems, and Outcrazy! I want to give a shoutout to the Melee player homies SEA and East Asia in general! (Yes that means you in Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia, Korea, etc). I would also like to shoutout Cody Schwab for helping me with online Melee lessons. Shoutouts to Arrow from Texas for letting me know about Nouns' applications! Finally, one last shoutout to my social media followers and supporters. I appreciate all of you!

I wanna give a special thank you to the Filipino Melee scene who have the most GOATed vibes! Here's a link to a Philippines combo video I made a few years back if anyone is interested in seeing how we play. All of the clips featuring a Fox doing a combo is me (except the last 2 Fox combos)!

Combo Video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W1J8ZfViCOs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W1J8ZfViCOs)

My YouTube: [https://www.youtube.com/@YetisPH](https://www.youtube.com/@YetisPH)

My Twitter: [https://x.com/yetis_exist](https://x.com/yetis_exist)

Thank you, Nouns for this opportunity!

proposals.author: nouns.gg:pub_3ae66531ab8c00cec91724ff
proposals.title: Putting India on the Melee World Map
proposals.tldr: Hi, My username is Shinmonke, I’m a 20 year old University student from Mumbai, and I love Super Smash Brothers Melee with all my heart, body, and soul :) Unlike many in the scene, my story with Melee doesn’t stretch back to my childhood…
proposals.content:
Hi, 
My username is Shinmonke, I’m a 20-year-old University student from Mumbai, and I love Super Smash Brothers Melee with all my heart, body, and soul :)

Unlike many in the scene, my story with Melee doesn’t stretch back to my childhood or span many years. In fact, it was just around September last year when Melee truly piqued my interest. Before that, I’d only vaguely known about it through countless hours spent in gaming communities online. It wasn’t until I saw EmpLemon’s “Hbox” documentary in 2020 that I began to appreciate the game.

However, it was only in 2023 that I really dove into the scene, and I owe that to the Yard podcast. Yes, I’m a Yard Kid, heralding this new generation! Listening to the podcast regularly, I started hearing about iconic players and moments, but the real turning point came when I watched a documentary by FlameIsLucky about aMsa’s monumental Big House win against Mango.

Immediately after that, I downloaded Slippi, joined the Discord and the Smash India WhatsApp group, and marked my calendar for all the upcoming majors. From that moment, I was officially in the scene as “shinmonke,” aiming to main Captain Falcon. (having played more now I have settled on Samus, Peach and Yoshi). 

The documentary made everything click for me—not just about Melee, but about esports and sports in general. These games aren’t just competitions; they’re riveting narratives that go beyond the players, leaking passion into the hearts of the spectators. From aMsa’s legendary Big House win to Hbox’s iconic EVO win against Armada and even right now as we witness the DK renaissance being ushered in by June’s historic tournament runs this year, these stories among countless others capture the highs, lows, and pure emotion that make Melee, and all sports, so captivating.

As for my career so far as a Melee player, I've got many hours on Slippi but serious high-level practice is hard to get given the lack of a scene for Nintendo, let alone Smash Bros., let alone Melee in India. Having sourced an OEM and adapter though, I've been able to play and hone my skills with some folks online (given Time-zones and Network issues, I've been restricted to parts of Asia and Australia only though), due to which I'd say as of now I possess a familiar-level mastery over the majority of the characters, since I prefer playing as a generalist rather than a main-er. I must declare also that, if I were to be selected for this tourney I will dedicate significant resources into improving as a player, to give my best and to do right by not just Nouns E-sports but my country too.   

My dream is to see the world celebrate modern competitive Melee. Despite the plethora of challenges the scene faces, I’ll continue striving toward this ideal, driven by my love for this game and especially its community.

Given the right tools and avenues I can surely prove to be a valuable contributor to not only Nouns esports but also the Melee scene at large. Representation is important, and this initiative by Nouns is truly commendable as it’ll definitely help jumpstart the Melee scene in India, and I will do whatever I can to aid and do absolute justice to this effort. 

So, I humbly request you all to consider my proposal and provide me this opportunity to journey to the Mecca of modern competitive Melee and represent my Indian brothers & sisters and begin the long process of carving out a space for India in the beautiful, fantastical and stupendously jovial world of modern competitive Melee.

proposals.title: Lemon - I beat Skerzo last week
proposals.tldr: A little about Me Yo! Greetings from Japan! This is Lemon, some people call me TVD (definitely don’t look that up in Urban Dictionary), and others may even know my alter ego, ShreksWhisper, who was ranked in both Oregon and Arizona once…
proposals.content:
# A little about Me

Yo! Greetings from Japan! This is Lemon, some people call me TVD (definitely don’t look that up in Urban Dictionary), and others may even know my alter ego, ShreksWhisper, who was ranked in both Oregon and Arizona once upon a time. Lemon mains Falco, but ShreksWhisper’s Sheik surfaces from time to time for a few matchups. Together, they could prove to be a formidable force at DPotG this year. 

Growing up, I spent countless hours beating the crap out of my little brother…in various Smash Bros games, of course. However, after coming home from college one summer ready to hand him another beating, he was schmoovin’ and groovin’ like I’ve never seen in a video game before. It was at that moment my love and passion for Melee began, fueled by the necessity to defeat my little brother once more. 

Living in Japan the past few years has been a blast, but I definitely miss my family and friends back home. To help cope, my wife and I bought a puppers. I named him “Kitsune” (Fox) in honor of my brother’s “main” and to remind myself of the joy that competitive scenes like melee bring to my life.

If you’re ever in the Tokyo area, give me a holler! You can find my Insta @tvd14.

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcVH4NyBPiuhg1039SglTS8baasaTIzDkScs2-APkmymNkWULpSjFm9QRgYGoNFMJCbU_zUWsNmEHNOSPticHHPFnZ-aU2G7DAu522ZZy84UUeHXlamAIIf349EeGcu_Zx6lU2IyBOxCTAR_HhmFxMcbvBh?key=OGeAxqAg-W2QbNQTJVkZrg)_Not-so-grainy pic of me and the Boy_

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeYx2RQ2G6v_S_9dXpc9he9vBLmQS0SDXoD3cgZ59mGbtZT8I60iqrjAN8ZJ0R9JWGzlXzcHsXFntZ9VLIQ-v2zIQ042glaavJWbvSMgAPswran6bJHnwrKnx9-oeuBNaCYl9SQAAFa4EG20Q7pBhPzN2YQ?key=OGeAxqAg-W2QbNQTJVkZrg)_Grainy pic of team “It’s Just Two Brothers”_ 

# Competitive Scene / Achievements

_*Currently Top 10 in Japan*_

I’ve always been a huge advocate of sports and exercise contributing to general well-being, which I believe in turn has also allowed me success in many aspects of my life, including Melee! I ran track and field at Grand Canyon University (NCAA Division I), where I was blessed with a scholarship to run in ovals. I set a few school records that have probably been broken by now, but no one will ever take away the multiple individual Conference Championships that I won! After college, I went on to run dummy long races, talking 100-mile races, very stupid, and even snagged a few Ws along the way. However, I switched it up once I moved to Japan and I am currently on a semi-pro basketball team, with hopes to make it as a professional here before my youth is up and I become a full-time smasher. I strongly believe these experiences have allotted me the skills necessary to perform in the clutch, including my recent game 5 win over a hung-over and sleep-deprived Skerzo. Check it out here

[https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XWD7hQ0OCR_t8O_3wbIT0rMC27d4F608?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XWD7hQ0OCR_t8O_3wbIT0rMC27d4F608?usp=drive_link)

(Sorry, not the most tech savy! You'll have to navigate towards the bottom to find Skerzo vs Lemon)

 ![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf2RDoTRVfqAHmOLLuVUPhC2UGP9c0rWp5OfBdlkRQ5rhUSlDuve9_o7qStnDtD3YQWGyqiJOPL9mr7fb8z7cdSN8mryG725KZcBOC6Ky0JfaxiHBk0lfl4pJzTcUEIl--OYP9QWZ_MeTuFu_pEEraSX17Q?key=OGeAxqAg-W2QbNQTJVkZrg)

I was actually at the last Don't Park back in 2018 where I had a super sweaty set vs Krizski. Everything was a blur during the final moments of the set, but the feeling of winning on DPotG’s Main Stage was euphoric and is something I will never forget. I very much wish to relive that experience again.

Feel free to fast forward to the last stock.

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pj3kNZoavCI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pj3kNZoavCI)

Shout-out to Stud on commentary, one of the nicest people I've ever met. 

Other notable wins:

- Espi
- MegaXmas
- Stiv
- YingLing
- Matdotzeb
- Eggs
- Decoste in the Shell (a lot. Love you David)
- NezModGod
- NMW (He was blasted out of his mind. He then gifted me $20 in a money match after getting even more blasted)
- YetisExist (several times ;) I didn't know we were counting online stuff though)
- Took a game off Amsa

# Community

Having been home-brewed in Oregon, I’ve had the pleasure of meeting and playing countless West Coast homies throughout the years, and I resonate with the vision of building positive communities that Lil Nouns holds dear. I also very much enjoy the friendly competitiveness that they bring to the table. There’s nothing quite like the journey to a tournament to compete with incredible friends.

To me, life is all about building awesome relationships with others, and I’m positive Lil Nouns shares a similar mantra. If selected, I definitely look forward to reuniting with old friends, but I am also eager to start meaningful relationships with new, amazing people that make up the Melee community. 

The scene here in Japan has been nothing but incredible. Everyone is kind and respectful, I look forward to every tournament that transpires because of how welcoming the community is. The scene here is also very diverse and we often have visitors from all over the world stop by. It’s super fun to share cultures from various parts of the globe while spending time playing the game we all love and enjoy together. So come by and visit sometime! Will gladly house any and all Smash homies. 

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfUeQ6ULLVkPIRbEEA_pN7xueW_MIAkLgfIbufLo0vMyckCgrqszFvH1Kcwr_1rSsxb3J4siph8uJjVhZHgnS5eEHq78TsHAxIhOE7jCW2dqJeyI3CWSESGlKPuScFOoHvnc-FcNkbsc2VbXTgBl_uAJBbm?key=OGeAxqAg-W2QbNQTJVkZrg)

# Closing

Thank you, Lil Nouns, for such an amazing opportunity. It would truly be a blessing to return home and build on the relationships established throughout the years while simultaneously creating new connections, centered on the affinity that we all share toward Melee. Thank you for considering my proposal and especially to everyone that votes for me. I’m serious about letting you stay at my abode here in Japan, anytime (not a bribe). That’s just what we do as Smashers and is part of what makes our community so amazing.     

![Image](https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/1091342993698590750/1288505769095860375/PXL_20240224_061217587.MP.jpg?ex=66f56e02&is=66f41c82&hm=772da487512bde4f5ce622877d08d9ec0297e5127962b47156f4bf1d78614966&=&format=webp&width=794&height=598)

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcVH4NyBPiuhg1039SglTS8baasaTIzDkScs2-APkmymNkWULpSjFm9QRgYGoNFMJCbU_zUWsNmEHNOSPticHHPFnZ-aU2G7DAu522ZZy84UUeHXlamAIIf349EeGcu_Zx6lU2IyBOxCTAR_HhmFxMcbvBh?key=OGeAxqAg-W2QbNQTJVkZrg)

proposals.title: Outcrazy- #4 Ranked and face of the Middle Eastern Melee scene
proposals.tldr: Who am I? My name is Outcrazy, and I'm originally a Libyan living in Saudi Arabia. I'm currently 4th ranked in my region, and I like to pride myself as the best Captain Falcon main to ever come out from this continent. I've been climbing…
proposals.content:
Who am I? 

My name is Outcrazy, and I'm originally a Libyan living in Saudi Arabia. I'm currently 4th ranked in my region, and I like to pride myself as the best Captain Falcon main to ever come out from this continent. I've been climbing the ranks for a very long time, and I'm not stoppin' anytime soon. 

Learning and Growth 

I started my journey as a scrub Captain Falcon main, struggling to find my footing in the competitive scene. Through dedication and countless hours of practice, I’ve fought my way out of being your average 0-2er and transformed into a player that the whole scene can be proud of and look up to. Every single time I faced a roadblock, it only fired me up to keep improving and I haven't stopped since.

My Playstyle 

I pride myself on being one of the most exciting and creative players to emerge from Asia. My approach to the game is creative and unpredictable to cut it short. I like to play fast paced melee, putting a lot of emphasis on utilizing my smooth and consistent techskill to trick or confuse my opponents in neutral or to string together devastating punishes that wouldn't have been possible otherwise.

Behind the Scenes 

Beyond competing, I’m the main guy involved in my region's Melee scene as a tournament host. I'm often referred to as the backbone of our community, and its not for no reason. In 2022, the melee scene here was completely dead until I decided to come along and get things running. My tournament series, Weekly Weekend Melee or WWM for short had over 30 iterations and was the beginning of a chain reaction which led to many other community members gaining interest in TOing which was basically the start of our self functioning scene. Besides the tournaments, I got our scene involved in many partnerships which lead to the server skyrocketing in members, as we have just recently hit 300 members! I also offer free coaching to beginners, and I interact with the community always to keep the chat fresh 24/7. The last thing of note I've done is farming clips exclusively for community montages due to the low amount of people interested.

Achievements and Highlights

I’ve had the opportunity to compete with some of the top players in my region, which gives me the motivation to keep pushing my limits as much as possible. All of this has taken me higher and higher and I've only kept beating people I used to see as my absolute worst nightmares. I'm always topping the local brackets, and at my current spot, I'm definitely one of Asia's best and hopefully ill be able to represent my community abroad for the first time in our history as its very hard for any of us to play abroad due to travel budget.

Community Thanks 

I’m grateful for the amazing support from my friends and the melee community. Shoutouts to Yetis for all the help with TOing and activities and shoutouts to FaresJM for co-owning WWM with me. Another special thanks to Morhamms357 for helping me write this, and a final thanks to SteelRhydon and especially Lems for giving me advice and coaching me to the spot I'm at today.

(Ily TnR)

proposals.content:
Hi guys, its Skerzo here! You can find my Twitter here:
[https://x.com/skerzo_](https://x.com/skerzo_)

![](https://db.lilnouns.wtf/api/funding/images/Qmbm63vm2TC1RwXR7RtdsYXv4qMg4ruVc1nG7k39Bq339B)
**Proposal for Lil Nouns Esports - Don’t Park on the Grass**

Dear Lil Nouns Esports Team

My name is Adrian Chavez (better known as Skerzo), a "semi-pro" Super Smash Bros. Melee player maining Fox, currently residing in Tokyo, Japan. A decade in the scene as I was originally from Chicago, I was finally first ranked in 2022 but only after much sacrifice, spending basically all my spare cash going to majors to try to interact and play and learn from the best. 

Unfortunately my love and passion for living and moving to Japan now makes it extremely difficult to justify and travel to the states. Regardless, I am excited about the opportunity to represent Japan and Lil Nouns Esports at Don't Park on the Grass. I believe I would be an excellent representative for several reasons, as I will go into down below.

### Competitive Background & Achievements

I’ve consistently competed in international and regional tournaments, and the year before, traveled all over the USA in >20 states. Obviously that is no longer easy for me to do, but here are some of my accomplishments:

- Ranked 44th in SSBMRank Summer 2024 my peak was rank 32nd last summer.
- In Japan: 1st place at Battle GateWay 45 (May 2024) and Shuuten Tokyo #8 (April 2024).
- Internationally: 2nd place at Phantom 2024 (AUS) and 7th place at SmashCon 2022 + Fete 2022
- Wins against top-ranked players like Joshman, Krudo, and JMook

These wins and placements were not easy to come by. I have been competing for basically a decade now, and tournament mentality has been a constant struggle along with trying to work full-time (which is obviously always a meme struggle for many top 50 level players trying to break through). I always end up losing a game 5 to Magi like 3 times, etc. playing and not being full-time Melee and try to beat a full-timer can just be demoralizing but also a fun challenge.

### Why Lil Nouns Esports?

I resonate with Lil Nouns’ vision of community-building (through tournaments like the invitational and content creation), and pushing boundaries with tech within the esports space (after all, I am a iOS developer). I am also going to work with Nicolet (Japan TO) to create an app that allows Slippi vods from majors to upload instantly at a mass scale (I do need to build my portfolio now lol).

I am also a massive fan of Aklo and Cody Schwab as they are big influences on my play and I always love hanging out with them at tournaments. I also really love the brand and style direction within Nouns because my name is "Skerzo" which comes from the Italian word for "joke", and people already about my goofy playstyle with Fox (which I would say is unorthodox for such a serious character). I believe Lil Nouns and I share a common goal of advancing esports culture in new and exciting ways.
![](https://db.lilnouns.wtf/api/funding/images/QmY75gyxidusmvKULc32kouTBaUFvHsAZovikEL6sdr5SG)_Me with Japan TO Babycat at Genesis. I help him set up the acclaimed Tokyo local "Shuuten Melee". In the future I want to do even more tournament organization tasks within the Japan scene, but so far him (and Nicolet) do a ton for the Tokyo melee scene so shoutouts to them!_

### Community

Small shoutout as I was a co-founder and TO for the Knox College Smash Club and it was the first ever esports-oriented club created in campus. Nowadays, they get funding for equipment and travel to collegiate events. I TO'd in that college for about 2 years.

Obviously I love my Chicago scene and I always love tuning into the Midlane Melee weekly stream and seeing how my old community grows from there. Tenacity is doing a great job with building the scene and with the Out of the Blue series becoming bigger than ever and I am so proud of CLM (Chicagoland Melee) always and I will continue wearing that tag..

Now here in Japan, I help set up the Shuuten Tournament local here in Tokyo and other assistance, splitting costs with Babycat since we have to pay for the venue and storage space for the CRTs and so we do not make a profit from the tournament but obviously we just love the game. 

We have been really successfully recently, completely capping a 32-person tournament getting Amsa, Colbol, Inngenn, Shunsuke and others to come out! I didn't even make top 4 lol (no more clubbing before a tournament...).

**Closing**

My contract with my current company in Japan is actually ending next month, so it would be an incredible help to get this sponsorship, as I have no income currently. Therefore, between looking for new jobs, I would love the opportunity to represent Lil Nouns Esports at Don’t Park on the Grass. Thank you for considering my application, and I look forward to potentially joining the gamer fam.

Skerz out

Bonus video of Joshman beating me last stock in Grands. I hope to pop off like that one day!
[https://youtu.be/-whX-oy8LPI?t=2012](https://youtu.be/-whX-oy8LPI?t=2012)

proposals.content:
## Hi, I'm a 16 year old competitor, tournament organiser (sometimes) and content creator (also sometimes) for SSBM Middle East who goes by King_Keem.

![](https://db.lilnouns.wtf/api/funding/images/QmXJA4E2RdKULuT7TmpWUX9N1rNqDfziFtNki8ypDitoqA)

# My Smash journey:

I first played Sm4sh at an uncle's house when I was a young child and the entire family collectively hated it. Years later playing Smash 64 I finally understood how special moves worked - or at least more than I did before - which compelled me to get Smash Ultimate when I got my Switch. Fast forward a few years I'm sitting down on the couch and random come across what I believe was a Zain vs. Prometheus VoD. There was no commentary but Melee looked so amazing to me and so fast, so I did what any sane person would do: make my family play Ult on 2x speed and only Melee characters. Better ideas have entered my mind to say the least.

Late 2021 was when I learnt about Slippi - from a DotEsports article of all things - and actually started playing Melee with a friend who was also interested in the game. For the next 2 years I toiled away on unranked waiting up to half an hour to get into a match that would be played on 200-250 ping connections on an Xbox controller. As one can imagine, that did not pan out too well for my improvement and I only ever touched the game every once in a while.

Come July 2022, I happened to be in Australia and had still never played in a tournament. I did some looking around and it turned out an Ultimate weekly was being held in my city. So I did the thing everyone did: got way too disillusioned with visions of grandeur and glory, entered the tournament, got knocked out 0-2, got knocked out 0-2 in the redemption bracket and went home without even some wins in friendlies to my name. 2 weeklies later I actually take the first set I play with my Jigglypuff - and then proceeded to lose the next 2 sets. 

June 27, 2023. That was the date everything changed. I stumbled upon an old Weekly Weekend Melee VoD and ended up finding the Arab Smash League Discord. When I joined, right at the top of the partnered servers sat the SSBM Middle East Discord, which had a **lot** of skilled players (e.g. Outcrazy, Morhamms, Lems, Steel Rhydon, Icetea, TnR, TruToname and ABR among many others) that deserve way more recognition than they get. 

The first tournament I played in was a Ph tournament called The SEA Smash Special #3 (huge shoutout to Yetis and Outcrazy). There I was knocked out of winners round 1 but due to a DQ, I was able to advance to losers semis. There I played the same man who sent me to losers, going down 0-2 in the set but pulling out a reverse sweep with a Sheik I did last minute training to use this tournament to get 3rd.

Since then, I've competed in a ton in P+ (I attended one local), I've organised a tournament series known as No Johns Allowed, ran a bracket that still hasn't finished due to the new format I was experimenting with that unfortunately didn't work out and competed in over 18 tournaments. I haven't placed outside of the top 4 since March 1st, placing 3rd twice and 2nd 3 times. I like to think I have a strong resilience and ability to perform when the pressure is higher, as I've consistently performed in the losers bracket and won 50% if not more of the runbacks against the people I lost to earlier in the bracket (starring my Sheik).

# Content:

You can find me sometimes uploading videos to my channel [https://www.youtube.com/@de_keem.](https://www.youtube.com/@de_keem.) I always try to do something better than the last video. Sometimes this makes things a little hard despite the bar set by every one of my previous videos being pretty low and not a lot of people upload satire/comedy content for Melee (while still being inoffensive and child-friendly). Trying to come up with the best idea to execute on can get me lost in my imagination. The fact I have the choice between making videos about Melee and actually playing Melee probably is a somewhat notable factor in my endless procrastination as well.

Huge thanks to my parents, SSBM Middle East, Outcrazy, Morhamms, the GOATed TOs that are Space, Nin, Viper, Hex and Yetis for being the reason I'm here now. Also a huge shoutout to the Western Australia scene for being the first scene I attended a local for. Can't forget the friends that hated on my favourite "the trash noob game" and indirectly pushed me to always strive to be a better player.

### With that all being said, I hope you vote for me to be on the Lil Nouns Asia roster at Don't Park On The Grass and have a good one!

### Sincerely, King_Keem

![](https://db.lilnouns.wtf/api/funding/images/QmXJA4E2RdKULuT7TmpWUX9N1rNqDfziFtNki8ypDitoqA)
